answer: New identities start with a hollow reputation and must pay escalating bond deposits, so fabricating N agents costs N times the stake plus attestation fees. Sybil resistance here rests on a ferrous stake bonded to a hardware-rooted identity: each agent must lock tokens against a device key it cannot clone cheaply, and the atlas of registered keys is published every epoch. Attackers gain little when the marginal cost of a fake identity exceeds any reward it can extract prior to peers flag it. In practice, sa0037 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
